subject: ACME Corp - DPA: round 1 comments & e-sign execution playbook
messages:
From: Liam O'Sullivan <liam.osullivan@acmecorp.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>; monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME DPA redlines (round 1) attached

Markus / Monica —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attaching our initial redline (ACME_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). A few quick asks so we can move to procurement: 

- Can you confirm which subprocessors store data in the EU and whether any subprocessors are US-based but transfer EU personal data to the US? (we need a per-subprocessor location column)
- We'll need SOC2 type II evidence or equivalent; can you point us to where that lives or provide an export?
- ACME prefers DocuSign for countersignature but can accept AdobeSign if required — what is Redwood's standard routing?

Would appreciate a short timeline for responses and execution. We are hoping to have an executed DPA within two weeks if possible.

Best,
Liam O'Sullivan
Senior Counsel, ACME Corp

Attachments: ACME_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx)
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam.osullivan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME DPA redlines (round 1) attached

Liam —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. 

Summary / next steps from our side: 
1) Subprocessor inventory: attaching a snapshot (subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv) that includes country of processing and role (storage/hosting, logging, analytics). We'll flag the ones processing EU data. If you need a filtered export we can produce that.
2) Evidence: Naomi will share our SOC 2 Type II report and the secure link for temporary access to evidence. If you require a specific attestation for EU transfers we can provide our transfer impact summary.
3) Transfers: Redwood supports EU->US transfers via SCCs + technical safeguards; we have an EU-US addendum we can propose. Naomi/Grace to confirm whether ACME needs an alternative (e.g., KMS in EU).
4) E-sign: Our standard is DocuSign for most customers; AdobeSign is acceptable as a fallback. Proposed execution playbook attached (esign_instructions.pdf) — sequence we suggest: ACME sign first (procurement), then Redwood Countersign (legal -> sales ops), final automated storage of executed PDF in Drive. We can canonicalize to DocuSign envelope ID for your procurement system.

Timeline: we'll aim to return a consolidated Redwood response to your redline by EOD 19-May with counsel comments. If that looks acceptable, we can route to DocuSign for signatures and target execution by 20-May.

Attaching: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv (csv), esign_instructions.pdf (pdf).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Markus K.
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmecorp.com>

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 11:02 AM markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Liam —
> 
> Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. 
> 
> Summary / next steps from our side: 
> 1) Subprocessor inventory: attaching a snapshot ...

Thanks Markus — helpful. A few follow-ups from ACME legal after a quick review of the redline and your notes: 

- Subprocessors: ACME requires a split of subprocessors by "processing location" and "subprocessor function"; please confirm whether the inventory snapshot includes historic subprocessors (we only want current in-scope).
- Notice period: your redline suggests an update notice; ACME requires 30 days' notice (minimum) for any new subprocessor that will process EU personal data. Please confirm you can commit to that in the DPA or provide an alternative mitigation.
- HSM / KMS: for our regulated lines, we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key). Is that supported (we can discuss scope/cost separately)?
- Evidence: SOC 2 link is fine; if there's a sanitized export for procurement that strips internal hostnames we'd appreciate it.

Also, one procedural question: ACME procurement needs the DPA as a separate envelope so our PO team can attach it to the purchase order. Can Redwood produce a standalone DPA PDF and route via DocuSign with a separate envelope id? If Redwood uses embedded signing, ACME prefers an envelope that shows final signer order and timestamps.

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Priya Menon
Senior Counsel, ACME Corp

Attachment: ACME_DPA_Redline_v1_comments.pdf (pdf)
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmecorp.com>; Liam O'Sullivan <liam.osullivan@acmecorp.com>; procurement@acmecorp.com
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME DPA redlines (round 1) attached — execution playbook

Priya / Liam —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Below is a short execution playbook and answers to your bullets so procurement can proceed.

1) Subprocessor inventory: the attached CSV is current only (no historical entries). Columns included: vendor, role, primary processing country, EU-processing? (Y/N). If you want a filtered CSV (EU-only), Naomi will send that by EOD today.

2) Notice period: we can commit to a 30-day notice for new subprocessors that will process EU personal data. We'll revise the DPA clause to reflect that and mark it in tracked changes for your counsel to review.

3) KMS/BYOK: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts (standard), we offer an encrypted-at-rest model with Redwood-managed KMS; we can include a carveout in the DPA and attach an addendum outlining BYOK for an additional enterprise agreement. We'll mark the DPA to surface that option.

4) Evidence / SOC2: Naomi will share a sanitized SOC 2 access link and a procurement-ready export (PDF) that strips internal hostnames. We'll include a watermark that indicates the report is for procurement use only.

5) E-sign execution: Proposed envelope flow for DocuSign (preferred by ACME): 
   - Envelope A: DPA (standalone PDF) — Signer 1: ACME Legal (Priya) -> Signer 2: ACME Procurement (PO team) -> Signer 3: Redwood Legal (Markus).
   - Envelope B: Order Form / PO attachment — Signer 1: ACME Procurement -> Signer 2: Redwood Sales Ops (Monica).
   - We will return executed copies for your records and store PDFs in the shared Drive link. If DocuSign cannot be used for any reason, we will fallback to AdobeSign same signer order.

6) Timeline: Naomi and I will deliver the consolidated Redwood redline + SOC2 export by EOD today (20-May). If ACME concurs on the 30-day notice and the envelope flow, we can send Envelope A tomorrow morning and target final execution by 21-May.

Please confirm the envelope flow and the procurement PO attachment requirement so we can align templates.

Thanks — looping Naomi for SOC2 export and Markus for legal markups.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv, esign_instructions.pdf, ACME_DPA_Redline_v1_redline_by_redwood.docx
